hunks.baseline: The easiest place to start was an inn or a pleasure house.
hunks.sol: The easiest places to start were inns and pleasure houses.

hunks.baseline: They were packed with all kinds of people from all kinds of professions, so you could hear countless stories just by listening a little.
hunks.sol: They were full of people from every walk of life. Listen for a while and you could hear all kinds of stories.

hunks.baseline: The downside was that none of the important information was there. Most of it was unverified rumor.
hunks.sol: The trouble was, there was rarely anything important among them. Most were unverified rumors.

hunks.baseline: So martial artists with heads that weren’t just for decoration, and who’d spent some time earning their keep with a sword, went to information merchants instead.
hunks.sol: So martial artists whose heads weren’t just for decoration, and who’d spent some time earning their keep with a sword, went to information merchants instead.

hunks.baseline: And so, the paths of those with money, a respectable sect behind them, and a few useful connections naturally split in two.
hunks.sol: For people with money, a respectable sect behind them, and a few useful connections, that left two natural choices.

hunks.baseline: They had taken root throughout the land. The weeds of this world, gathering one by one until they’d grown into vast forests of their own.
hunks.sol: They had taken root throughout the land. The weeds of this world had gathered one by one and grown a vast forest of their own.

hunks.baseline: The Beggars’ Sect was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, so there was no need to explain its importance. But the Lower District Sect was a force that couldn’t be dismissed, either.
hunks.sol: The Beggars’ Sect was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, so its importance went without saying. But the Lower District Sect couldn’t be dismissed, either.

hunks.baseline: Like the beggars of the Beggars’ Sect, they were everywhere in the world.
hunks.sol: Like the beggars of the Beggars’ Sect, they were everywhere.

hunks.baseline: With such vast networks, they combed the land and hauled in information by the basketful. Even the Sect Leaders of the most prestigious Murim sects couldn’t treat them carelessly.
hunks.sol: Their vast networks let them cast a net across the land and haul in a wealth of information. Even the Sect Leaders of the most prestigious Murim sects couldn’t treat them carelessly.

hunks.baseline: “Gather everyone. You have half a day. To the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
hunks.sol: “Gather everyone. You have half a day. At the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

hunks.baseline: “Quietly plant yourself in a corner and sit there. You need to hear this, too.”
hunks.sol: “Plant yourself quietly in a corner. You need to hear this, too.”

hunks.baseline: “I, Bicheonja of the Qingcheng Sect, a junior of the Murim, pay my respects to you, Senior.”
hunks.sol: “This junior, Bicheonja, pays his respects to you, Senior.”

hunks.baseline: Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect or not, in front of Jeok Cheongang, he was a junior of the Murim.
hunks.sol: Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect or not, before Jeok Cheongang, he was a junior.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: Bicheonja was clearly fresh from a desperate, sweat-soaked dash. Jeok Cheongang nodded at his cupped-fist greeting. No—at the greeting of Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, as he was better known in the Murim.
hunks.sol: Bicheonja looked as though he’d run hard enough to sweat through his soles. Jeok Cheongang nodded at his cupped-fist greeting. Bicheonja—or Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, as he was better known in Murim.

hunks.baseline: No, maybe it was more accurate to say he let it slide because his opponent was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
hunks.sol: No, it was probably more accurate to say he let it slide because this was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: There was no one in the Murim who could match his seniority, and he was overwhelming in both age and martial arts.
hunks.sol: No one in Murim could match Jeok Cheongang’s seniority, and his age and martial arts were overwhelming.

hunks.baseline: But Extinction Divine Nun, who’d taken the vacant post of Emei Sect Leader after the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, was someone even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t treat carelessly—at least, given her age.
hunks.sol: But Extinction Divine Nun, who’d taken the vacant post of Emei Sect Leader after the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, was someone even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t treat carelessly, given her age.

hunks.baseline: I pressed a hand to my forehead, while everyone else’s mouths fell open.
hunks.sol: I pressed a hand to my forehead. Everyone else’s mouths fell open.

hunks.baseline: At least there was one saving grace: Extinction Divine Nun, who was famous for rampaging like a madwoman on the battlefield, was usually an exceptionally gentle person.
hunks.sol: At least there was one saving grace: Extinction Divine Nun, famous for rampaging like a madwoman on the battlefield, was usually an exceptionally gentle person.

hunks.baseline: “Benefactor Jeok, you’re just as I remember you, no matter how long it’s been. In more ways than one.”
hunks.sol: “Benefactor Jeok, you’re the same whenever I see you. In more ways than one.”

hunks.baseline: Of course, Jeok Cheongang wouldn’t have just let her hit him. The important thing was that Extinction Divine Nun’s anger quickly subsided when I appeared.
hunks.sol: Of course, Jeok Cheongang wouldn’t have just let her hit him. What mattered was that her anger quickly subsided when I appeared.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “You needn’t be so formal. Call me whatever feels comfortable. In any case, you’ve become even more striking since I last saw you. And your hair’s still so thick.”
hunks.sol: “You needn’t be so formal. Call me whatever feels comfortable. In any case, you’ve become even more striking since I last saw you. And such a full head of hair.”

hunks.baseline: Extinction Divine Nun added that last part while glancing at Jeok Cheongang, then patted my shoulder with her wrinkled hand.
hunks.sol: Extinction Divine Nun added that last part while looking at Jeok Cheongang, then patted my shoulder with her deeply wrinkled hand.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps because she’d thought so highly of the way I’d rushed around trying to minimize the damage during the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, both she and Cheongpung the Ancient Sword were looking at me with stars in their eyes.
hunks.sol: Perhaps because she thought so highly of the way I’d rushed around trying to minimize the damage during the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, both she and Cheongpung the Ancient Sword looked at me so fondly their eyes might as well have been dripping honey.

hunks.baseline: Word had already spread among those with even a halfway decent information network. And that went double for the people gathered here today.
hunks.sol: The story had already begun making the rounds among people with decent information networks. And that certainly included everyone gathered here.

hunks.baseline: Two Sect Leaders from the Nine Sects and One Gang, not to mention the heads of the most powerful information organizations in the land.
hunks.sol: Two Sect Leaders from the Nine Sects and One Gang, not to mention leaders of the land’s foremost information organizations.

hunks.baseline: “Congratulations, though belated, Great Hero Jin Taekyung. Our Shaanxi Branch Leader was delighted when he heard the news.”
hunks.sol: “Congratulations, though belatedly, Great Hero Jin Taekyung. Our Shaanxi Branch Leader was delighted when she heard the news.”

hunks.baseline: “I only wish that brat Gung Gibang—or rather, the Successor Beggar—could follow your example, even halfway. Anyway, what you did was incredible.”
hunks.sol: “I only wish that brat Gung Gibang—or rather, the Successor Beggar—could measure up to you even halfway. Anyway, what you did was incredible.”

hunks.baseline: “Where’s the Sect Leader? Why’s some no-name Elder hanging around?”
hunks.sol: “Where’s your Sect Leader? Why’s some mere Elder hanging around?”

hunks.baseline: “……Sir Jeok, even so, how could we bring the Sect Leader from Henan in half a day?”
hunks.sol: “……Sir Jeok, how could we bring the Sect Leader here from Henan in half a day?”

hunks.baseline: “Henan? Is that bastard in Henan right now?”
hunks.sol: “Henan? That bastard’s in Henan right now?”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang seemed to accept that the Elder had a point and started looking for another target.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang seemed to accept that the Elder had a point and looked for another target.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, you. Lower District Sect.”
hunks.sol: “Hey. Lower District Sect.”

hunks.baseline: “Where’s the Sect Leader?”
hunks.sol: “Where’s your Sect Leader?”

hunks.baseline: “I’d be more than happy to bring him here, but even I don’t know where he is. Our sect is organized into cells, so his location is top secret…”
hunks.sol: “I’d dearly love to bring him here, but even I don’t know where he is. Our sect is organized into cells, so his location is a closely guarded secret…”

hunks.baseline: “So a nobody who doesn’t even know where his own Sect Leader is showed up?”
hunks.sol: “So you sent some nobody who doesn’t even know where his Sect Leader is?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course not. Whatever information you want, we’ll get it by any means necessary and bring it to you as quickly as we can!”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. Whatever information you want, we’ll find it by any means necessary and bring it to you as quickly as we can!”

hunks.baseline: “Whatever you want. By any means necessary. As quickly as you can?”
hunks.sol: “Whatever I want. By any means necessary. As quickly as you can?”

hunks.baseline: “That sounds pretty good. I’ll remember it clearly, so you remember this one thing, too. Understand?”
hunks.sol: “That sounds good. I’ll remember it clearly, so you remember this one thing, too. Understand?”

hunks.baseline: The Lower District Sect Branch Leader’s eyes wavered. Just then, Jeok Cheongang’s voice rang out, low and heavy.
hunks.sol: The Lower District Sect Branch Leader’s eyes wavered. Then Jeok Cheongang’s voice sounded, low and heavy.

hunks.baseline: The terrifying wave of energy that rolled out from Jeok Cheongang was a wordless warning—a precaution against the unlikely but possible mishap.
hunks.sol: The terrifying wave of qi that rolled out from Jeok Cheongang was a wordless warning against the slightest chance of a leak.

hunks.baseline: They all understood that something important was about to be discussed.
hunks.sol: They understood, too, that something important was about to be discussed.

hunks.baseline: I added quietly, “There’s no room for suspicion. It’ll be reported as a natural death. At least, officially.”
hunks.sol: I added quietly, “A death by illness, beyond all suspicion. That’s how it will be reported. Officially, at least.”

hunks.baseline: Anyone could tell those words carried weight. They implied a secret that wasn’t meant to reach the outside world.
hunks.sol: Anyone could hear the implication. That one word told them there was a secret the outside world didn’t know.

hunks.baseline: At my subtle glance, the Divine Physician nodded, took a small wooden case from his robe, and carefully opened it.
hunks.sol: At my quiet glance, the Divine Physician nodded, took a small wooden case from his robe, and carefully opened it.

hunks.baseline: The people who saw it stared wide-eyed. It was smaller than any bug I’d ever seen, and red as spilled blood.
hunks.sol: The people who saw it stared wide-eyed. It was smaller than any insect I’d ever seen, and red as blood.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang and I were the only ones left. We stood together, looking out at the pitch-black darkness all around us as we talked.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang and I were the only ones left. We talked as we looked out at the pitch-black darkness that had settled all around us.

hunks.baseline: “If we take one wrong turn, it’ll take even longer to get back. Besides, haven’t we already gained something from their information?”
hunks.sol: “One wrong turn, and it’ll take even longer to find our way back. Besides, haven’t we already learned something from their information?”

hunks.baseline: No one living in this land could fail to recognize that name.
hunks.sol: No one living in this land could fail to know that name.

hunks.baseline: In Anhui Province, not Zhejiang Province, where the Great Nation’s capital and the Emperor’s residence were located.
hunks.sol: In Anhui Province, not Zhejiang Province, where the Imperial Capital and the Son of Heaven resided.

hunks.baseline: Why had the Embroidered Uniform Guard—an agency directly under the Emperor—appeared in Anhui Province, even changing their identities?
hunks.sol: Why had the Embroidered Uniform Guard—an agency directly under the Emperor—appeared in Anhui Province with their identities concealed?

hunks.baseline: We had no way to learn more. The informants who’d caught their scent and followed them had been found dead. But I couldn’t help making a grim assumption.
hunks.sol: We had no way to learn more. The informants who’d caught their scent and followed them had been found dead. But I couldn’t help imagining the worst.

hunks.baseline: The only vassal king in the land, and—since the Son of Heaven had no heir—the current successor to the Great Nation’s throne.
hunks.sol: The only vassal king in the land and, with the Son of Heaven having no heir, the current successor to the Great Nation’s throne.

hunks.baseline: If their destination was Shanxi Province… I couldn’t help anticipating the worst.
hunks.sol: If their destination was Shanxi Province… I could only foresee the worst.

hunks.baseline: That the shadow of Dark Heaven had reached the Great Nation’s imperial family.
hunks.sol: The shadow of Dark Heaven had reached the Great Nation’s imperial family.

hunks.baseline: *The Captain of the Guards said the City Lord of Sichuan Province had started showing signs of madness after the Son of Heaven took his favorite concubine. And the Blood Soul Gu found in his body was so rare that I’d never even seen one in the Poisonblood Grounds in Nanman.*
hunks.sol: *The Captain of the Guards said the City Lord of Sichuan Province had started showing signs of madness right after the Son of Heaven took his favorite concubine. And the Blood Soul Gu found in his body was so rare that I’d never even seen one in the Poisonblood Grounds in Nanman.*

hunks.baseline: There was enough evidence. I silently stared up at the night sky, lit only by the hazy moonlight.
hunks.sol: There was enough evidence. I silently stared up at the night sky, lit only by hazy moonlight.

hunks.baseline: A question that would reach no one.
hunks.sol: The question I wanted to ask would reach no one.

hunks.baseline: And then, at that very moment—
hunks.sol: And then—

hunks.baseline: No. It reached both our ears.
hunks.sol: No. It reached both of us.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t the wind. Something was flying toward us, beating its wings through the air.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t the wind. It was the beating of wings as something flew through it toward us.

hunks.baseline: The moment I realized it, Jeok Cheongang and I both looked toward the distant sky. Our eyes widened.
hunks.sol: The moment I realized it, Jeok Cheongang and I looked toward the distant sky. Our eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: The shadow of a bird raced toward us, slicing through the wind. There were more than ten of them.
hunks.sol: The shadows of more than ten birds raced toward us, cutting through the wind.
